A Gondorian citadel of the White Mountains' passes: austere quarters, disciplined hospitality, and the cold clean air of the heights. A traveller of standing sleeps safe under the banner of the Stewards.

Sleeping within Fangorn means lying among roots that seem to shift when unwatched; the wood is awake and aware of the intruder. No fire feels wise here. The dark is deep, the creak of timber close and deliberate, and rest comes shallow under the attention of something ancient and unhurried.
A Gondorian palace where a guest of rank is lodged in tapestried chambers, dined with ceremony and attended by servants. Magnificent and safe, if a little stiff with etiquette.
A Gondorian fortress: a cot in the barracks, army rations, and the changing watch through the night. Austere and orderly, safe behind thick walls though broken by the guard's tread.
A Gondorian watchtower on the marches: a bunk in the guardroom, a soldier's supper, and the beacon ready above. Cramped and vigilant, safe under watching eyes.
A Gondorian farming village gives plain hospitality: a corner of the barn or a let room, bread and cheese and cautious courtesy. The settled land is safe and the night passes quietly.
Whatever shelter a lonely Gondorian steading or shrine affords: a plain roof, simple food, and the quiet of the tilled country. Rest is simple and safe.
A sober Dunadan town of the north: a plain, clean inn kept by grave folk who ask little, a firm bed and simple fare. Dignity and a quiet melancholy hang over the half-empty streets of a fading realm.
A walled Dunadan town of the north, its gate barred against the wild. The inn is spare and orderly, the welcome grave; behind the ramparts a traveller sleeps safe in a watchful land.

A Dunadan city of the old north-kingdom, grander in memory than in fact: stone guest-halls, plain good food, and the grave courtesy of a proud, dwindling people. Safe and dignified beneath the weight of lost Arnor.
A walled Dunadan city of the north, its concentric ramparts enclosing orderly streets. Lodging is secure and grave; the men are tall and solemn, heirs of Numenor keeping the long watch.
A lonely Dunadan waystation of the north road: clean, plain, and orderly, the host asking no questions. A firm bed and a quiet night in a haunted, empty country.

A night on Dagorlad is a night on a graveyard: flat trampled waste and peat-reek, the ground littered with the bones of old battle, cold mist curling low. Sleep is fitful, broken by the sense of things half-seen at the edge of the eye, and the dead lie close beneath.
A Dunadan manor of the north: a guest-bed, a solemn supper, and the grave hospitality of a noble house that remembers better days. Restful and safe, if touched with melancholy.
A Dunadan lord's castle of the north: a seat at the long table, meat and bread, a bed in the guest-range. Grave and formal, safe behind old stone, cold with the memory of Arnor.
A Dunadan keep of the marches: a plain cell, soldier's fare, the watch changing through cold hours. Spare and vigilant under the eyes of the Rangers.
A Dunadan citadel holding the old borders: austere, watchful, its small garrison grave and disciplined. Safe but cheerless in a land under threat.
A Dunadan fortress of the north: a bunk in the guardroom, plain rations, the long watch. Austere and safe, kept by silent, capable men.
A Dunadan watch-post of the north: a cot in a cold tower, a Ranger's spare welcome, the dark country watched below. Safe under vigilant eyes.
A Dunadan steading of the north takes the traveller in warily but honourably: a place by the fire, a share of the pot, a bed of straw. Grave border-folk, but the welcome is true.
A lonely Dunadan croft or old waymark of the north: plain shelter, simple food, and the haunted quiet of a country that was once a kingdom.
A Northman town thick with woodsmoke and horse-smell, its hall-inn loud with the talk of herders and rivermen. Mead, roast meat, and a bench or a pile of hides to sleep on among a hardy, open people.
A Northman trading-town grown large on river and road: a busy hall-inn, mead and meat and boasting late into the night, and a warm if noisy place to sleep among horse-folk and merchants.

To sleep in Lothlorien is to rest as if outside of time. The mallorn-light lingers gold into the dusk, the air is clean and still, and no evil thing walks here. Weariness lifts and the heart grows quiet; a traveller wakes lighter than he lay down.
A Northman hall-inn by the road: smoke, mead, roasting meat, and a place by the long-fire. Warm and loud, the welcome rough and genuine.
A Northman chieftain's hall of timber and thatch, where a traveller is feasted or weighed by the season's mood. Mead and meat and firelight; warm, loud, and safe among friends.
A Northman lord's steading, half-hall half-farm: a seat at the fire, a hearty supper, a bed of hides. Proud independent folk, generous once trust is given.
A Northman fortified hall on the plains: earthwork and timber, a warm smoky interior, mead passed round the fire. Rough but safe, the welcome open to a proven friend.
A Northman village of the grass or river-land: a family hall of straw and peat, a bowl of stew, a bed of hides. Wary of strangers but warm once you are let in.
A Northman war-camp or stockade: earthworks, a rough barracks, plain fare and the watch on the palisade. Spare and vigilant against raiders, but safe within.
A lone Northman herder's camp or river-jetty: a fire, a share of the pot, the wide dark of the plains. Rough hospitality under an open sky.

A Hobbit town such as Bree-folk know: a cheerful inn with a roaring hearth, more supper than a tall man expects, dark ale and soft (if short) beds. The talk is all crops, cousins and neighbours; sleep comes warm and easy.
A Hobbit family takes the traveller in, half from kindness, half from curiosity: a place by the kitchen fire, a heaped plate, a bed of quilts in a round-doored smial. Warm, genuine, deeply peaceful.
A snug Hobbit inn: low beams, a roaring fire, endless courses of supper and excellent ale. Beds soft if short; a traveller sleeps warm and wakes well-fed.

The remnant holds the keep: a few families of the old dependants who never left, gates shut, smoke from one corner of the yard. If they let you in — and they weigh you at the door first — the night is stone walls, a shared pot and the strange safety of people who decided staying was worth it.
text.es: El remanente sostiene la fortaleza: unas pocas familias de los viejos dependientes que nunca se fueron, puertas cerradas, humo de un solo rincón del patio. Si te dejan entrar — y primero te miden en la puerta — la noche es muros de piedra, una olla compartida y la seguridad rara de gente que decidió que quedarse valía la pena.

text.en: A town dying by inches, but dying people still keep fires. The few hundred who remain crowd into the quarter that still has roofs; a shared hearth is offered plainly, without ceremony — the hospitality of those who know what an empty street looks like.
text.es: Un pueblo que se muere de a poco, pero la gente que se muere también mantiene fuegos. Los pocos cientos que quedan se apretujan en el barrio con techos; se ofrece un hogar compartido de manera llana, sin ceremonia — la hospitalidad de quien conoce cómo se ve una calle vacía.

text.en: One house inside the ring of Fornost still has people in it — a family that kept the roof and the door while everything around them became the Deadmen's Dike. Their fire is small and real; outside it, the dark is older than they are.
text.es: Una casa dentro del anillo de Fornost todavía tiene gente — una familia que conservó el techo y la puerta mientras todo alrededor se volvía los Cercas de los Muertos. Su fuego es chico y real; afuera, la oscuridad es más vieja que ellos.

text.en: The inn is half a ruin, but the stables are not empty — a family lives in the part that still stands and takes a traveller in out of the same weather. A dry corner, a shared pot, and a wall between you and the old north-kingdom's night.
text.es: La posada es media ruina, pero las cuadras no están vacías — una familia vive en la parte que sigue en pie y recibe al viajero por el mismo mal tiempo. Un rincón seco, una olla compartida y una pared entre vos y la noche del viejo reino del norte.

text.en: The ford-settlement is shuttered, but the old inn keeps fresh ash and hidden provisions for men who never give their names. A traveller the grey cloaks don't mind gets a dry floor and a night without questions — the safest sleep in southern Ithilien, if you can find who's keeping it.
text.es: El asentamiento del vado está cerrado, pero la posada vieja guarda ceniza fresca y provisiones escondidas para hombres que nunca dan su nombre. Un viajero que no molesta a las capas grises consigue un piso seco y una noche sin preguntas — el sueño más seguro del sur de Ithilien, si encontrás quién lo guarda.

text.en: The tower above the ford is held by whoever holds it this year — hard men, or worse. If you sleep inside it is because they allowed it, and you sleep the way you do among armed strangers: with a roof, a wall and one eye open.
text.es: La torre sobre el vado la tiene quien la tiene este año — hombres duros, o peor. Si dormís adentro es porque lo permitieron, y dormís como se duerme entre desconocidos armados: con techo, con pared y con un ojo abierto.

text.en: The citadel of the hill-folk is a court of clan, not kingdom — but a fire in a great hall is a fire. Taken in by the door's judgement, a guest gets the bench, the pot and the rules; sleep comes easier inside walls that have held for a thousand years.
text.es: La ciudadela de la gente de las colinas es una corte de clan, no de reino — pero un fuego en un gran salón es un fuego. Admitido por el juicio de la puerta, un huésped recibe el banco, la olla y las reglas; el sueño viene más fácil dentro de muros que aguantan desde hace mil años.

text.en: The dunir who stayed inside the old fort keep its stone patched and its fields worked. Their welcome is slow — they watch from the wall a long while first — but the roof is real and the pot is shared once the door decides.
text.es: Los dunir que se quedaron dentro del viejo fuerte mantienen la piedra remendada y los campos trabajados. Su bienvenida es lenta — miran desde el muro un buen rato primero — pero el techo es real y la olla se comparte una vez que la puerta decide.

text.en: The little village sits on the bones of a much bigger town — mud-and-wood huts among old foundations, rough people, an open fire. They take in travellers the way border people do: plainly, and with questions. The dead city around them is just stone; the living part is warm.
text.es: La aldeíta se asienta sobre los huesos de un pueblo mucho más grande — chozas de barro y madera entre cimientos viejos, gente tosca, un fuego abierto. Reciben al viajero como lo hace la gente de frontera: llanamente y con preguntas. La ciudad muerta alrededor es solo piedra; la parte viva es tibia.

text.en: An old hobbit-village where most windows go dark at dusk — but the families that remain keep their smials the way hobbits do. A traveller who is let in gets a low ceiling, a full table and the deep quiet of a hole dug into good earth.
text.es: Una aldea hobbit envejecida donde la mayoría de las ventanas se apagan al atardecer — pero las familias que quedan mantienen sus smials como los hobbits saben hacerlo. Un viajero admitido recibe un techo bajo, una mesa llena y la quietud profunda de un agujero cavado en buena tierra.

text.en: The big stone building at the crossroads keeps one family where an inn used to keep dozens — and they keep the old customs too: a fire in the hearth, a pot that is always on, a bed for anyone the door decides to like. It is less than it was, and more than the road offers anywhere else for miles.
text.es: El edificio grande de piedra en el cruce conserva una familia donde antes una posada alojaba a docenas — y conservan las viejas costumbres también: fuego en el hogar, una olla siempre puesta, una cama para quien la puerta decide querer. Es menos de lo que fue, y más de lo que el camino ofrece en millas a la redonda.

label.en: Trade the countersign for news
label.es: Cruza la contraseña por noticias

text.en: He answers the way rangers answer rangers — everything, in order, and the truth about the ugly parts: the bandit sign at the third milestone, the washout under the south ford, the weather the peaks are keeping back. The man pays in the same coin: the names of the two pulled north, and the stretch of hills one pair of eyes now watches where three used to keep it. They part as the watch parts — quickly. 'Clear road to you,' the ranger says, which among rangers is as close to a blessing as the road gets.
text.es: Responde como responden los montaraces entre sí — todo, en orden, y la verdad sobre lo feo: la señal de bandidos en el tercer mojón, el desprendimiento bajo el vado del sur, el tiempo que los picos vienen guardando. El hombre paga en la misma moneda: los nombres de los dos llamados al norte, y el tramo de colinas que ahora vigila un par de ojos donde antes lo cuidaban tres. Se despiden como se despide la guardia — rápido. «Buen camino», dice el montaraz, que entre los suyos es lo más parecido a una bendición que ofrece la ruta.

label.en: Offer his own road-report first
label.es: Ofrecer primero su parte del camino

text.en: He offers his own report before the man can ask for it — the sign on the south road, the state of the fords, the weather the peaks are holding back. A ranger who gives before he takes is read correctly: in return come the gap in the patrol, the two missing men, and a warning about the stretch beyond the last hill. 'I have not had the legs to walk it myself,' he says, and for a man who walks all day, that is the whole confession.
text.es: Ofrece su propio parte antes de que el hombre pueda pedírselo — la señal en el camino del sur, el estado de los vados, el tiempo que los picos vienen guardando. Un montaraz que da antes de tomar es leído correctamente: a cambio vienen el hueco en la patrulla, los dos hombres perdidos, y una advertencia sobre el tramo tras la última colina. «No me han dado las piernas para caminarlo yo mismo», dice, y para un hombre que camina todo el día, esa es toda la confesión.

label.en: Nod to a fellow watcher and keep moving
label.es: Saluda a otro de la guardia y sigue

text.en: A raised hand between men of the same watch — news can wait for a road that has none to spare. The ranger does not press; he knows what an empty circuit costs better than anyone. The traveller carries the sight of him alone on the ridge for the rest of the day.
text.es: Una mano alzada entre hombres de la misma guardia — las noticias pueden esperar para un camino que no tiene a quién dárselas. El ranger no insiste; nadie sabe mejor que él lo que cuesta un circuito vacío. El viajero se lleva la imagen de ese hombre solo en la cresta por el resto del día.

label.en: Let the silence do the weighing
label.es: Dejar que el silencio haga el pesaje

text.en: He does not fill the silence after — lets the weight of the missing report sit between them, the way you let a bad track declare itself before naming it. The older man finally says what the silence was for: 'If he was taken, the cache locations are all that spoke.' Neither of them says the third reading. They do not need to.
text.es: No llena el silencio que sigue — deja que el peso del parte faltante repose entre ambos, como se deja que un mal rastro se declare antes de nombrarlo. El mayor dice por fin para qué era el silencio: «Si lo tomaron, las ubicaciones de los depósitos son lo único que habló». Ninguno dice la tercera lectura. No hace falta.

label.en: Offer to re-walk the cache line
label.es: Ofrecer recorrer la línea de depósitos

text.en: He offers to re-walk the cache line — check the stones, read who came, whether the taking was one man or several. The older ranger weighs it and shakes his head once: 'No. If it is rotten I want it found by the watch, not around it.' A hard answer, and an honest one.
text.es: Ofrece recorrer la línea de depósitos — revisar las piedras, leer quién vino, si lo que se llevaron fue cosa de uno o de varios. El montaraz mayor lo pesa y niega una vez con la cabeza: «No. Si está podrido quiero que lo encuentre la guardia, no sus alrededores». Una respuesta dura, y honesta.

label.en: Take the report and give no opinion
label.es: Tomar el parte sin dar opinión

text.en: He takes the report and offers no opinion — some sums are better carried than balanced on the spot. The older man accepts the discretion without comment; it is why he chose this one to tell.
text.es: Toma el parte y no ofrece opinión — hay cuentas que se cargan mejor que se saldan en el acto. El mayor acepta la discreción sin comentario; es por eso que eligió contárselo a éste.

label.en: Take the northern circuit
label.es: Tomar el circuito del norte

text.en: He runs the calculation honestly — what the northern detour costs in days, what it costs in arriving — and then agrees, because farms going dark in sequence is not a thing you decline to walk toward. 'The steadings empty in order,' the man says at parting. 'Whatever is doing it does not hurry. Do not let it hurry you either.'
text.es: Hace el cálculo con honestidad — lo que el desvío al norte cuesta en días, lo que cuesta en llegada — y luego acepta, porque granjas que se apagan en secuencia no son algo hacia lo que uno se niega a caminar. «Las haciendas se vacían en orden», dice el hombre al despedirse. «Lo que sea que lo hace, no se apura. No dejes que te apure a vos tampoco».

label.en: Counter with the tracker's split
label.es: Contraofrece con la división del rastreador

text.en: He counters with the tracker's answer: not the whole circuit — the last two farms' back-trails. 'I read the ground where they went dark, you keep the line south. Whoever finds the spoor, the other follows.' The man weighs it a moment and nods — the split covers less ground but reads it better.
text.es: Contraofrece con la respuesta del rastreador: no el circuito entero — los rastros de las últimas dos granjas. «Yo leo la tierra donde se apagaron, vos seguí la línea al sur. El que encuentre el rastro, el otro lo sigue». El hombre lo pesa un momento y asiente — la división cubre menos terreno pero lo lee mejor.

label.en: Decline — his own road has obligations
label.es: Declina — su camino tiene sus propias deudas

text.en: He declines — the road he is on is its own obligation, and he says so plainly. The ranger takes the refusal without argument; men on circuits learn early that a debt pressed is a debt refused twice. He is already looking south when the traveller goes.
text.es: Declina — el camino en que está es su propia obligación, y lo dice con franqueza. El montaraz toma la negativa sin discutir; los hombres de circuito aprenden pronto que una deuda presionada es una deuda rechazada dos veces. Ya está mirando al sur cuando el viajero se va.

label.en: Answer what she knows — and see the grandson
label.es: Responder lo que sabe — y ver al nieto

text.en: She answers what she knows — the steadings emptied in order, moving east, and families leave in order like that for one reason and it is not famine. Then, while he writes it into his report, she sees it plainly: the set of the jaw, the grey of the eye — the grandson of a man she knew, seventy years back. She does not say so. Some debts are better owed than declared.
text.es: Responde lo que sabe — las haciendas se vaciaron en orden, yendo al este, y las familias se van así en orden por una sola razón y no es el hambre. Luego, mientras él lo vuelca en su informe, ella lo ve con claridad: el corte de la mandíbula, el gris del ojo — el nieto de un hombre que conoció, setenta años atrás. No lo dice. Hay deudas que es mejor deber que declarar.

label.en: Ask, first, who his grandfather was
label.es: Preguntar, primero, quién fue su abuelo

text.en: She asks, before answering, who his grandfather was — the question surprises him into a name she already half-expected. 'He walked this stretch once,' she says, which is true, and gives him the news after that as something owed to the man he resembles.
text.es: Ella pregunta, antes de responder, quién fue su abuelo — la pregunta lo sorprende y le arranca un nombre que ella ya medio esperaba. «Caminó este tramo una vez», dice, que es verdad, y le da después las noticias como algo debido al hombre al que se parece.

label.en: Give the bare news and keep the resemblance
label.es: Dar la noticia escueta y guardarse el parecido

text.en: She gives him the bare news and nothing more — the resemblance is hers to keep, a private debt she does not mean to pay in words. He thanks her formally and goes, never knowing what stood behind the courtesy.
text.es: Le da la noticia escueta y nada más — el parecido es suyo para guardar, una deuda privada que no piensa pagar en palabras. Él agradece formalmente y se va, sin saber nunca qué había detrás de la cortesía.

label.en: Give him one true thing
label.es: Darle una sola cosa verdadera

text.en: She considers whether to answer fully — then gives him one true thing, small enough to carry: 'The songs are wrong about the dying. They make it sudden. It was slow, the way ice is slow — and people kept planting orchards anyway, because that is what you do when you intend to stay.' He stands very still while he files it. Then: 'Thank you,' he says, quietly — a man handed more than he asked for, and aware of it.
text.es: Considera si responder por completo — y luego le da una sola cosa verdadera, lo bastante chica para llevar: «Las canciones se equivocan sobre la muerte. La hacen repentina. Fue lenta, como es lento el hielo — y la gente seguía plantando huertos igual, porque eso es lo que uno hace cuando piensa quedarse». Él se queda muy quieto mientras lo archiva. Después: «Gracias», dice, bajo — un hombre al que le dieron más de lo que pidió, y lo sabe.

label.en: Give him the smaller kindness instead
label.es: Darle, en cambio, la bondad más chica

text.en: She gives him the smaller kindness instead: 'The land remembers better than I do, and the land is still here. Read it — it will not flatter you.' He receives the refusal like a correction from a teacher, and strangely it seems to be what he needed.
text.es: Le da, en cambio, la bondad más chica: «La tierra recuerda mejor que yo, y la tierra sigue acá. Leela — no te va a adular». Él recibe la negativa como una corrección de maestro, y extrañamente parece ser lo que necesitaba.

label.en: Answer nothing; some hungers stay hungry
label.es: No responder nada; hay hambres que quedan

text.en: She says nothing — the question is too large for a road, and some hungers are better left hungry. He nods as if he half-expected the silence, and the way he looks at the ruins on the way out says the asking cost him something anyway.
text.es: No dice nada — la pregunta es demasiado grande para un camino, y hay hambres que conviene dejar hambrientas. Él asiente como si medio esperara el silencio, y el modo en que mira las ruinas al partir dice que la pregunta le costó algo de todos modos.

label.en: Give him the minimum that is also true
label.es: Darle el mínimo que también es verdad

text.en: She recognizes real attention when it arrives — infrequent enough to register like weather changing. 'Well enough for the road,' she says, which is the minimum that is also true, and watches him receive it: he nods once, accepts the smaller answer for what it is, and does not press.
text.es: Reconoce la atención verdadera cuando llega — lo bastante infrecuente para registrarse como un cambio de clima. «Bastante bien para el camino», dice, que es el mínimo que también es verdad, y lo mira recibirla: asiente una vez, acepta la respuesta menor por lo que es, y no insiste.

label.en: Answer the question he asked, not the one he meant
label.es: Responder la pregunta que hizo, no la que quiso

text.en: She answers the question he asked, not the one he meant — the road, the weather, the walking — and lets him keep the larger one for someone who can answer it. He understands. The understanding is its own small mercy.
text.es: Responde la pregunta que él hizo, no la que quiso hacer — el camino, el tiempo, la caminata — y le deja guardar la más grande para alguien que pueda responderla. Él lo entiende. El entendimiento es su propia pequeña misericordia.

label.en: Let the question stand and walk on
label.es: Deja la pregunta en pie y sigue

text.en: She lets the question stand unanswered — a courtesy of its own kind, since anything she could say would be either a lie or a ledger he has not earned. He nods as though he expected nothing else, and lets the road take her.
text.es: Deja la pregunta sin respuesta — una cortesía propia, ya que cualquier cosa que pudiera decir sería una mentira o un libro que él no se ha ganado. Él asiente como si no esperara otra cosa, y deja que el camino se la lleve.

text.en: Watches them pass without speaking. Is not certain he could have.

label.en: Hear them out, and thank them in their own tongue
label.es: Escúchalos y agradécelos en su propia lengua

text.en: He takes the news standing, without interrupting — three days' silence on the Elven road, a stretch of it already searched. When he thanks them it is in Sindarin, the northern dialect, and something eases in the elf who answered: a Man keeping the old courtesy in the old tongue. 'Then look well along the road,' the nearest says at parting — and from their kind, on an open road, it is as close to trust as a stranger earns.
text.es: Recibe la noticia de pie, sin interrumpir — tres días de silencio en el camino élfico, un tramo ya registrado. Cuando agradece lo hace en sindarin, el dialecto del norte, y algo se afloja en el elfo que respondió: un Hombre guardando la cortesía antigua en la lengua antigua. «Entonces mira bien a lo largo del camino», dice el más cercano al despedirse — y viniendo de los suyos, en un camino abierto, es lo más parecido a la confianza que un extraño gana.

label.en: Offer to pass through the dead ground
label.es: Ofrece pasar por el tramo silenciado

text.en: He offers the one thing a lone Dúnadan can: his own eyes on the stretch they cannot cover. The elves weigh it — a Man offering to walk into whatever silenced a patrol — and accept with the courtesy kept for people who know what they are offering. 'We cannot cover it all,' the nearest admits, and the words plainly cost something. 'Walk the ground north of the second ridge. If there is a trail to find, it begins there.'
text.es: Ofrece lo único que un Dúnadan solitario puede dar: sus propios ojos en el tramo que ellos no pueden cubrir. Los elfos lo pesan — un Hombre ofreciendo entrar a lo que sea que silenció a una patrulla — y aceptan con la cortesía reservada a quien sabe lo que ofrece. «No podemos cubrirlo todo», admite la más cercana, y a las palabras claramente les cuesta salir. «Camina la tierra al norte de la segunda cresta. Si hay un rastro que encontrar, empieza ahí.»

label.en: Take the warning and keep walking
label.es: Toma la advertencia y sigue

text.en: He listens, and does not offer the help he is not sure he can give. Between long-lived peoples a refusal is information too, and the elves accept it as quietly as the warning was given. The dead stretch stays behind him, and travels with him.
text.es: Escucha, y no ofrece la ayuda que no está seguro de poder dar. Entre pueblos longevos una negativa también es información, y los elfos la aceptan con la misma calma con que dieron la advertencia. El tramo silenciado queda atrás, y viaja con él.

text.en: Tells them the direction but not the reason. There is kindness in not explaining.
Does not react immediately. Then asks: when. Listens to the answer.
Holds his gaze. Then: I know.
Reads the sign correctly. Leaves dried meat at the base of the marker stone. Walks on.
Notes where they stopped. Approaches the barrow with full attention.
Stops. Waits. Takes the longer path around.
Stops. Looks at the staff without pointing at it. Then meets his eyes.
Does not react to the token. Gives them the old sign. Waits.
Returns the sign. Asks with her hands: how recently. He holds up three fingers.
Gives him the road conditions precisely. Watches him update a small book.
Describes the shaft's location without mentioning the artifact. Watches the Dwarf decide whether to trust further.

label.en: Give him the old name of the pass
label.es: Darle el nombre antiguo del paso

text.en: The question is not strange to either of them: she was alive when Khazad-dûm still stood. She reads the map's first landmark — a mountain-pass that had two names before it had the one his people use now — and gives him the older one, the name Moria's own records kept. The dwarf copies it letter by letter, asks nothing of what she is, and pays her the highest compliment his kind owns: he does not doubt her word. 'Good,' he says — and for a dwarf thanking, that is nearly a speech.
text.es: La pregunta no es extraña para ninguno de los dos: ella estaba viva cuando Khazad-dûm aún existía. Lee el primer hito del mapa — un paso de montaña que tuvo dos nombres antes del que ahora usa su pueblo — y le da el más antiguo, el nombre que guardaban los propios registros de Moria. El enano lo copia letra por letra, no pregunta qué es ella, y le paga el mayor cumplido que tiene su gente: no duda de su palabra. «Bien», dice — y para un enano agradeciendo, eso casi es un discurso.

label.en: Ask what the vein is worth to him
label.es: Preguntar qué vale la veta para él

text.en: She asks, blunt in kind, what the vein is worth. The dwarf measures her the way a man measures a toll — then, surprisingly, answers: not gold. Iron, of a grain his charts say runs nowhere else this side of the mountains. Kin-metal, he calls it, and for a moment the map stops being paper and becomes a grave he is trying to visit politely.
text.es: Ella pregunta, igual de directa, qué vale la veta. El enano la mide como se mide un peaje — y, sorprendentemente, responde: no oro. Hierro, de un grano que sus cartas dicen no corre en ningún otro lugar a este lado de las montañas. Metal de parentesco, lo llama, y por un momento el mapa deja de ser papel y se vuelve una tumba que él intenta visitar con cortesía.

label.en: Plead a poor memory and move on
label.es: Alega mala memoria y sigue

text.en: She shakes her head at the map — too many names have died to keep them all. The dwarf takes the refusal with the same flatness he asked it, folds the chart away with care, and nods once. Some share of the mountain's memory walks on with her, unshared; he will never know how close it stood.
text.es: Niega con la cabeza ante el mapa — han muerto demasiados nombres para guardarlos todos. El enano acepta la negativa con la misma sequedad con que preguntó, guarda el mapa con cuidado y asiente una vez. Una parte de la memoria de la montaña sigue caminando con ella, sin compartir; él nunca sabrá qué tan cerca estuvo.

text.en: Does not ask what was in the passages. Asks where the western passages exit on the surface.
Says she was not there at the beginning. Tells him she knows who was. Watches what he does with that.
Does not slow. Does not make eye contact with the face in the bracken. Passes at normal pace.
Asks about the ford. Gets an answer, with conditions attached.

label.en: Take the description and add the cousin to the watch
label.es: Toma la descripción y suma al primo a su guardia

text.en: He has walked that ground and seen no hobbit camp east of the Hills — he says it plainly, because a soft answer would be a kind lie and the question deserves a true one. Then he asks what the cousin looks like, what he carried, which road he meant to take. 'Red hair, a green cloak, and he whistles when he's frightened,' the hobbit says — 'which, thinking on it, he likely is right now.' The traveller files it the way he files everything worth finding: hobbit-made camp, small fire, trade pack. If it lies within three days of here, his eyes will find it now that they know to look.
text.es: Ha caminado esa tierra y no ha visto ningún campamento hobbit al este de las Colinas — lo dice con franqueza, porque una respuesta suave sería una mentira amable y la pregunta merece una verdad. Luego pregunta cómo es el primo, qué llevaba, qué camino pensaba tomar. «Pelo rojo, capa verde, y silba cuando está asustado», dice el hobbit — «que, pensándolo bien, probablemente lo esté ahora mismo». El viajero lo archiva como archiva todo lo que vale buscar: campamento de hobbit, fuego pequeño, mochila de mercader. Si está a tres días de aquí, sus ojos lo encontrarán ahora que saben qué buscar.

label.en: Tell him plainly what lies east of the Hills
label.es: Decirle con franqueza qué hay al este

text.en: He tells the hobbit what the ground east of the Weather Hills is, in a ranger's plain terms — not to frighten him, because the hobbit deserves the real map. The hobbit listens, goes pale at exactly the right places, and does not turn back. 'I will keep to the road, then,' he says, which is almost courage.
text.es: Le cuenta al hobbit qué es la tierra al este de las Colinas de los Vientos, en los términos francos de un montaraz — no para asustarlo, porque el hobbit merece el mapa de verdad. El hobbit escucha, palidece exactamente en los lugares correctos, y no da media vuelta. «Me ceñiré al camino, entonces», dice, que es casi coraje.

label.en: See him as far as the next safe roof
label.es: Acompañarlo hasta el próximo techo seguro

text.en: He offers the hobbit his company as far as the next walled roof — three miles he was walking anyway. The hobbit talks the whole way: about the cousin, the trade pack, how the family said the east road was safe enough for hobbits now. He has rarely heard anyone be wrong so cheerfully, and he says nothing at all.
text.es: Le ofrece al hobbit su compañía hasta el próximo techo con paredes — tres millas que iba a caminar de todos modos. El hobbit habla durante todo el trayecto: del primo, de la mochila de mercader, de cómo la familia dijo que el camino del este ya era bastante seguro para los hobbits. Pocas veces ha oído a alguien equivocarse con tanto buen humor, y no dice absolutamente nada.

text.en: Picks up the apple. Sets it on a stone off the road so it is findable. Continues.
Sits down at the edge of the fire uninvited. Nobody objects.
Asks how close. He tells her. Recalibrates where she will camp.

label.en: Answer the cargo question, not the origin

text.en: He answers the question about cargo — plainly, completely, hands visible — and does not answer the question about origin, which the captain notices and lets pass, because the description says dispatches, not origins. 'On your way, then,' the captain says at last, stepping aside with the particular politeness of a man still not quite sure he should.
text.es: Responde la pregunta sobre la carga — con claridad, completa, manos visibles — y no responde la de origen, que el capitán nota y deja pasar, porque la descripción dice despachos, no orígenes. 'Seguí tu camino, entonces', dice el capitán al final, haciéndose a un lado con la cortesía particular de un hombre que todavía no está del todo seguro de que debería.

label.en: Answer the captain's question with a better one

text.en: He has already counted them and found the formation wanting — the left flank is too eager, the rear man too far back, the captain the only one priced correctly. So he answers the first question with a question of his own: 'Arthedain fell nine hundred years ago. Who is paying its bounties now?' The captain blinks — the question is too informed to ignore and too dangerous to answer. In the silence, the traveller has already won the only exchange that mattered.
text.es: Ya los contó y encontró la formación floja — el flanco izquierdo demasiado ansioso, el de atrás demasiado lejos, el capitán el único bien tasado. Así que responde la primera pregunta con una pregunta propia: 'Arthedain cayó hace novecientos años. ¿Quién paga sus recompensas ahora?' El capitán parpadea — la pregunta es demasiado informada para ignorarla y demasiado peligrosa para responderla. En el silencio, el viajero ya ganó el único intercambio que importaba.

label.en: Let the captain weigh his vague report

text.en: She lets him decide and does not help him decide — no courtesy offered, no indignation either; she simply stands in the road the way old things stand, while he measures the report against what is in front of him. 'Move along,' he says finally, professionally — a man who has decided that some forms are better left unfiled.
text.es: Lo deja decidir y no lo ayuda a decidir — sin cortesía ofrecida, tampoco indignación; simplemente se queda en el camino como se quedan las cosas viejas, mientras él mide el reporte contra lo que tiene enfrente. 'Seguí adelante', dice finalmente, profesional — un hombre que decidió que algunos formularios es mejor dejarlos sin llenar.

label.en: Wait out the captain's arithmetic

text.en: She has already counted them and identified what each will do — the left one's hand keeps drifting to his belt-knife, the right one is scared, the captain is the only professional. She waits for his decision, still as stone, and it is the stillness that finally wins: the captain recalculates, slowly, the cost of being wrong about her. 'Road's yours,' he says at last, stepping aside with a bow that costs him nothing and was meant to cost her nothing either.
text.es: Ya los contó e identificó qué va a hacer cada uno — la mano del de la izquierda no deja de ir al cuchillo del cinto, el de la derecha tiene miedo, el capitán es el único profesional. Ella espera su decisión, quieta como piedra, y es la quietud la que finalmente gana: el capitán recalcula, despacio, el costo de equivocarse con ella. 'El camino es tuyo', dice al final, haciéndose a un lado con una reverencia que no le cuesta nada y tampoco pretendía costarle nada a ella.

label.en: Answer them in the old manner

text.en: She has already decided, and lets them begin — the captain opens with the questions, the formation tightens on schedule, and she answers the first of them in a voice that has learned patience the way stone learns water. What she says is her name and her errand, in the old manner. Three of them do not understand what they have just heard. The fourth, the captain, understands just enough — and steps out of her road.
text.es: Ya decidió, y los deja empezar — el capitán abre con las preguntas, la formación se cierra según lo previsto, y ella responde la primera de ellas con una voz que aprendió paciencia como la piedra aprende el agua. Lo que dice es su nombre y su mandado, a la manera antigua. Tres de ellos no entienden lo que acaban de oír. El cuarto, el capitán, entiende lo suficiente — y se aparta de su camino.

label.en: Pay for the crossing in northern news
label.es: Pagar el vado con noticias del norte

text.en: He names what he knows from the north — the roads, the wrongness, what the watch has been finding — and watches her weigh it against the crossing's price. 'That will do,' she decides. 'The guide is a Stoor — marsh-blooded hobbit-kind, you will know him by the pole. Word to carry: the red-haired woman says the water owes him.' The deal closes the way marsh deals should — both sides sure they got the better of it.
text.es: Dice lo que sabe del norte — los caminos, lo que anda mal, lo que la guardia viene encontrando — y la mira pesarlo contra el precio del vado. «Con eso alcanza», decide. «El guía es un Stoor — sangre hobbit de la marisma, lo reconocés por la pértiga. Palabra para llevarle: la pelirroja dice que el agua le debe». El trato se cierra como deben cerrarse los tratos de la marisma — ambos lados seguros de haber ganado.

label.en: Ask about the guide before paying
label.es: Preguntar por el guía antes de pagar

text.en: He asks about the guide before paying — what a Stoor is doing keeping a Gwathuirim crossing, what the pole is for. 'He is ours the way the marsh is ours,' she says, 'by knowing it better than anyone argues with. The pole finds the channel where the mud hides it.'
text.es: Pregunta por el guía antes de pagar — qué hace un Stoor guardando un vado gwathuirim, para qué es la pértiga. «Es nuestro como la marisma es nuestra», dice ella, «por conocerla mejor de lo que nadie discute. La pértiga encuentra el canal donde el barro lo esconde».

label.en: Keep the news and find the crossing himself
label.es: Guardarse las noticias y hallar el vado solo

text.en: He keeps his news and finds the crossing himself — the river will tell him what her price would have bought, more slowly and wetter. She shrugs the trader's shrug: a deal declined is still a deal read correctly.
text.es: Se guarda las noticias y busca el vado por su cuenta — el río le dirá lo que el precio de ella habría comprado, más despacio y más mojado. Ella se encoge de hombros con el gesto del comerciante: un trato declinado también es un trato leído correctamente.

label.en: Carry the word north
label.es: Llevar la palabra al norte

text.en: He agrees to carry it — and specifies, out of honesty, what north means: the garrison at the cross-roads, three days if the fords hold, no promise of audience. 'A ranger's no-promise is worth more than most men's oath,' she says — and gives him the names, the farmsteads, the night the eastern clan's fires were seen moving. The message walks north with him now, and something in her shoulders unclenches a fraction.
text.es: Acepta llevarla — y especifica, por honestidad, qué significa norte: la guarnición del cruce de caminos, tres días si los vados aguantan, ninguna promesa de audiencia. «Una no-promesa de montaraz vale más que el juramento de la mayoría», dice — y le da los nombres, las haciendas, la noche en que se vieron mover los fuegos del clan del este. El mensaje ahora camina al norte con él, y algo en los hombros de ella se destensa una fracción.

label.en: Ask why her own people do not carry it
label.es: Preguntar por qué no lo llevan los suyos

text.en: He asks why her own people do not carry it — a fair question, asked to know the ground. 'A Gwathuirim bringing this word is a clan quarrel. A stranger bringing it is news.' She says it without bitterness, the way one reports the depth of snow — and he understands the whole of her politics in one sentence.
text.es: Pregunta por qué no lo llevan los suyos — una pregunta justa, hecha para conocer el terreno. «Un gwathuirim trayendo esta palabra es una pelea de clanes. Un extraño trayéndola es noticia». Lo dice sin amargura, como se reporta la profundidad de la nieve — y él entiende toda su política en una frase.

label.en: Decline plainly rather than cheaply
label.es: Declinar con franqueza, no con liviandad

text.en: He declines — his road has its own obligations, and he says so plainly rather than cheaply. She accepts it with a nod that has no hope left to lose, and turns her face back to the marsh.
text.es: Declina — su camino tiene sus propias obligaciones, y lo dice con franqueza y no con liviandad. Ella lo acepta con un gesto al que ya no le queda esperanza que perder, y vuelve la cara hacia la marisma.

label.en: Ask which way the lights move
label.es: Preguntar hacia dónde se mueven las luces

text.en: He asks which direction the lights move — the question of someone who believes her, which is already half the help she needed. 'East to west. Along the deep channel. Faster when nobody is watching.' He takes the answer and adjusts the route — not away from the bog, but with respect for what it has started showing. She exhales like a woman who has finally set something down.
text.es: Pregunta hacia dónde se mueven las luces — la pregunta de alguien que le cree, que ya es la mitad de la ayuda que ella necesitaba. «De este a oeste. Por el canal profundo. Más rápido cuando nadie mira». Él toma la respuesta y ajusta la ruta — no lejos del pantano, pero con respeto por lo que empezó a mostrar. Ella exhala como una mujer que por fin soltó algo.

label.en: Tell her the fear was right
label.es: Decirle que el miedo estaba bien

text.en: He tells her what the lights most likely are — and more importantly, that she was right to keep her people out. 'Fear with a reason is not fear,' he says. 'It is the marsh's fence, and you held it.' She does not smile, but she stands differently after — a woman whose fear has been made official.
text.es: Le dice qué son probablemente las luces — y más importante, que hizo bien en mantener a su gente afuera. «El miedo con razón no es miedo», dice. «Es la cerca de la marisma, y vos la sostuviste». Ella no sonríe, pero después se para distinto — una mujer cuyo miedo fue oficializado.

label.en: Hear it and give the honest small answer
label.es: Escucharla y dar la pequeña respuesta honesta

text.en: He listens to the end and gives her only the honest thing: 'I do not know this marsh well enough to name them. Do not let anyone go in after them.' Less than she hoped and more than she has — she nods, and keeps to the dry side of the road.
text.es: La escucha hasta el final y le da sólo lo honesto: «No conozco esta marisma lo bastante para nombrarlas. No dejes que nadie entre tras ellas». Menos de lo que esperaba y más de lo que tenía — asiente, y se queda del lado seco del camino.

label.en: Offer the company and take the crossing
label.es: Ofrece la compañía y toma el vado

text.en: He offers the company without being asked twice — it costs him nothing he was not already paying. They walk the exposed stretch in companionable silence, and at the settlement's edge she pays her side in full: the new crossing, marked by willows, knee-deep at low water. 'Ask for the Stoor,' she says. 'He will take you for a fish and a story.'
text.es: Ofrece la compañía sin que se lo pidan dos veces — no le cuesta nada que no estuviera pagando ya. Caminan el tramo expuesto en un silencio cordial, y al borde del poblado ella paga su parte completa: el nuevo vado, marcado por sauces, hasta la rodilla en marea baja. «Pregunta por el Stoor», dice. «Te cruza por un pescado y un cuento».

label.en: Ask the price of the crossing outright
label.es: Preguntar de entrada el precio del vado

text.en: He asks the price of the crossing outright — marsh deals are better stated than guessed at. 'Company to the settlement,' she says, and then, because the asking pleased her: 'And if you know who owned the drowned wagon — his wife still asks after him.'
text.es: Pregunta de entrada el precio del vado — los tratos de la marisma se dicen mejor que se adivinan. «Compañía hasta el poblado», dice ella, y luego, porque la pregunta le gustó: «Y si sabes de quién era la carreta ahogada — su mujer todavía pregunta por él».

label.en: Take the warning and walk on alone
label.es: Toma la advertencia y sigue solo

text.en: He thanks her for the ford-warning and walks on alone — a fair refusal, and she takes it as one, calling after him the only thing worth shouting: 'The willows, then — follow the willows!'
text.es: Agradece la advertencia del vado y sigue solo — una negativa justa, y ella la toma como tal, gritándole tras él lo único que vale gritar: «¡Los sauces, entonces — seguí los sauces!»

label.en: Notice the unsaid and ask for it
label.es: Notar lo no dicho y pedirlo

text.en: He notices what is not said — the pause where the useful news lives — and asks for it directly, the way her people respect. 'The crossing is at the willow-marked channel, a mile east,' she says, 'and you did not hear it from me — the clan that keeps it charges more than a smile.' She gives him the rest: a name, a word to carry, and the look of a woman who has decided her coin was well spent.
text.es: Nota lo que no se dijo — la pausa donde viven las noticias útiles — y lo pide directamente, del modo que su gente respeta. «El vado está en el canal marcado por sauces, una milla al este», dice, «y no lo oíste de mí — el clan que lo guarda cobra más que una sonrisa». Le da el resto: un nombre, una palabra para llevar, y la mirada de una mujer que decidió que su moneda fue bien gastada.

label.en: Pay first, in northern news
label.es: Pagar primero, con noticias del norte

text.en: He pays before asking — the state of the northern roads, a dry route east she can sell twice. The marsh respects a man who pays first; she gives him the crossing, the name, and a bonus the withholding would never have bought: 'Tell the keeper the red-haired woman sent you. It buys the dry crossing, not just the wet one.'
text.es: Paga antes de preguntar — el estado de los caminos del norte, una ruta seca al este que ella puede vender dos veces. La marisma respeta a un hombre que paga primero; ella le da el vado, el nombre, y un extra que la reticencia jamás habría comprado: «Decile al guardián que te manda la pelirroja. Te compra el cruce seco, no sólo el mojado».

label.en: Take the free news and leave the priced
label.es: Tomar la noticia gratis y dejar la de precio

text.en: He thanks her for the bad news and leaves the actionable news unsold — a clean transaction, honestly ended. She watches him go with the respect of a trader whose silence was read correctly.
text.es: Agradece la mala noticia y deja la útil sin vender — una transacción limpia, terminada con honestidad. Ella lo mira partir con el respeto de una comerciante cuyo silencio fue leído correctamente.

label.en: Tell her the truth about the lights
label.es: Decirle la verdad sobre las luces

text.en: He lets the silence last a beat first — the answer deserves the weight — then: 'I know what those lights are. I will not tell you it is safe to go near them, because it is not.' Something in her face settles at the truth rather than the comfort — the marsh folk respect a straight answer the way dry-landers respect a roof.
text.es: Deja que el silencio dure un compás primero — la respuesta merece el peso — y después: «Sé qué son esas luces. No te voy a decir que es seguro acercarse, porque no lo es». Algo en su cara se asienta con la verdad y no con el consuelo — la gente de la marisma respeta una respuesta directa como los de tierra seca respetan un techo.

label.en: Question the lights before naming them
label.es: Interrogar las luces antes de nombrarlas

text.en: He asks about the lights before judging them — how they move, whether they answer movement, what they did the night before the men went in. Her answers are precise; marsh people are excellent witnesses to things they fear. 'You ask like a tracker,' she says — and gives him the rest she had been holding.
text.es: Pregunta por las luces antes de juzgarlas — cómo se mueven, si responden al movimiento, qué hicieron la noche anterior a que entraran los hombres. Sus respuestas son precisas; la gente de la marisma es excelente testigo de lo que teme. «Preguntás como un rastreador», dice — y le da el resto que se había estado guardando.

label.en: Give no name he is not sure of
label.es: No dar un nombre del que no está seguro

text.en: He gives her nothing — not yet sure enough of the lights to put a name on them, and a false name in the marsh is worse than none. She reads the withholding for what it is and lets him pass, colder than before, but unhurt.
text.es: No le da nada — todavía no está lo bastante seguro de las luces para ponerles nombre, y un nombre falso en la marisma es peor que ninguno. Ella lee la reserva por lo que es y lo deja pasar, más fría que antes, pero ilesa.

label.en: Ask what he's studying, then go with him

text.en: He asks what the man is crouched over — 'Something's been taking animals from the high pasture. There and gone by midday. No tracks.' He already asked his neighbours; they refused, and asking a stranger costs him what pride he has left. The traveller goes with him — and up on the pasture they find what 'no tracks' means: the kill-sites are clean because whatever feeds there does not leave the ground. It leaves the sky. 'The neighbours,' the herdsman says, 'will hear about this from someone braver than me.'
text.es: Pregunta qué está mirando el hombre — 'Algo se viene llevando animales del pastizal alto. Está y se fue al mediodía. Sin rastros.' Ya les preguntó a los vecinos; se negaron, y preguntarle a un extraño le cuesta el poco orgullo que le queda. El viajero va con él — y arriba en el pastizal encuentran lo que 'sin rastros' significa: las matanzas están limpias porque lo que se alimenta ahí no deja el suelo. Deja el cielo. 'Los vecinos', dice el pastor, 'se van a enterar de esto por alguien más valiente que yo.'

label.en: Ask what the paper says

text.en: He stops and asks what the paper says — and the man produces it like a confession: a Gondorian road-permit issued to his father, long expired. 'Where would the nearest garrison reissue one?' The traveller answers plainly — the town's name, and that they reissue in person, no penalty for the asking. 'In person,' the man repeats, tasting the phrase like a man who had expected to be arrested.
text.es: Para y pregunta qué dice el papel — y el hombre lo produce como una confesión: un permiso de ruta gondoriano extendido a su padre, vencido hace tiempo. '¿Dónde lo renovaría la guarnición más cercana?' El viajero responde sin vueltas — el nombre del pueblo, y que lo renuevan en persona, sin multa por preguntar. 'En persona', repite el hombre, saboreando la frase como un hombre que esperaba ser arrestado.

label.en: Read the old stones' inscription for him

text.en: She asks which stones — and as he describes them, she knows exactly what they are: boundary markers of a people the Gondorians built over, predating the kingdom's survey by an age. She tells him what the inscription says — the boundary formula, the old names, what the marks under the lichen once declared. He writes it all down with hands that shake slightly, twice stopping her to spell a name. 'Two years,' he says at the end, quietly — as though accounting for the time itself.
text.es: Pregunta qué piedras — y mientras él las describe, ella sabe exactamente qué son: mojones de frontera de un pueblo sobre el que los gondorianos construyeron, anteriores al relevamiento del reino por una era. Le dice lo que la inscripción dice — la fórmula de lindero, los nombres viejos, lo que las marcas bajo el liquen declararon alguna vez. Él lo anota todo con manos que tiemblan apenas, deteniéndola dos veces para deletrear un nombre. 'Dos años', dice al final, en voz baja — como rindiendo cuentas del tiempo mismo.

label.en: Ask the symptoms, give what she knows

text.en: She asks what the symptoms are — and listens while he lists them, then asks about the mine shaft: how deep, how old, what was worked there. The answers fit something older than a healer's book. She gives him what he needs — the name of a plant, the words for what it does, and a warning to keep the sick out of the dark — without explaining how she knows it. He does not ask that either. Desperate men know which questions cost extra.
text.es: Pregunta cuáles son los síntomas — y escucha mientras él los enumera, después pregunta por el pozo de la mina: qué profundo, qué viejo, qué se trabajó ahí. Las respuestas encajan en algo más viejo que un libro de curandero. Ella le da lo que necesita — el nombre de una planta, las palabras para lo que hace, y la advertencia de mantener a los enfermos lejos de la oscuridad — sin explicar cómo lo sabe. Él tampoco lo pregunta. Los hombres desesperados saben qué preguntas cuestan extra.

label.en: Ask what holds him at the fork

text.en: She stops and asks what the east fork holds. 'The mine,' he says, without turning. Then, because she stopped when no one stops: 'I was a healer's apprentice at the outpost up there, before the Plague closed it. They sealed the mine with men still in it, some of them. I have been old longer than they were allowed to be.' Whatever is in that shaft, she understands, he has been carrying it longer than any traveller should.
text.es: Ella para y pregunta qué tiene la bifurcación del este. 'La mina', dice él, sin darse vuelta. Después, porque ella paró cuando nadie para: 'Yo era aprendiz de curandero en el puesto de allá arriba, antes de que la Plaga lo cerrara. Sellaron la mina con hombres adentro, algunos de ellos. Llevo siendo viejo más tiempo del que a ellos les dejaron ser.' Lo que haya en ese pozo, ella entiende, él lo viene cargando más de lo que ningún viajero debería.

text.en: Reads the territorial mark. Adjusts the route to skirt the claim.

label.en: Give them the true answer
label.es: Darles la respuesta verdadera

text.en: He names himself for what he is — Dúnedain of the North, no friend of Gondor's tall men — and watches three faces do the arithmetic. One relaxes; the speaker does not, not entirely; the third looks back down the road as if measuring whether a lie would have run faster. 'North-man,' the speaker repeats at last, tasting the word for the lie in it and finding none. 'Pass, then — and keep to the road.' Whatever the correct answer was, he seems to have given it.
text.es: Se nombra por lo que es — Dúnadan del Norte, no amigo de los hombres altos de Gondor — y mira tres rostros hacer las cuentas. Uno se relaja; el que habla no, no del todo; el tercero mira el camino detrás como midiendo si una mentira habría corrido más rápido. «Hombre del Norte», repite por fin el que habla, paladeando la palabra en busca de la mentira y no hallándola. «Pasá, entonces — y cebíte al camino». Cualquiera haya sido la respuesta correcta, parece haberla dado.

label.en: Ask what the answer is worth on this road
label.es: Preguntar qué vale la respuesta en este camino

text.en: He asks, flat, what the answer buys on this stretch. The speaker approves of the question — men who ask the stakes before answering pay them more honestly. 'Clan ground,' he says. 'A claim older than your kings' maps — and a southern cloak out here burns like a lantern at night. Answered?' The traveller walks on knowing the rule of the road he is on.
text.es: Pregunta, sin adornos, qué compra la respuesta en este tramo. Al que habla le gusta la pregunta — los hombres que preguntan la apuesta antes de responder suelen pagarla con más honestidad. «Tierra de clan», dice. «Un derecho más viejo que los mapas de tus reyes — y una capa del sur acá arde como un farol de noche. ¿Contestado?» El viajero sigue su marcha conociendo la regla del camino que pisa.

label.en: Keep walking; let them do the reading
label.es: Sigue caminando; que lean ellos

text.en: He gives them nothing — no name, no halt, only the measured pace of a man who is not running from three. They grant him the calculation in return: a man who will not answer is also an answer, and not the dangerous kind. He feels their eyes on his back until the next rise takes him.
text.es: No les da nada — ni nombre, ni alto, sólo el paso medido de un hombre que no está huyendo de tres. Le conceden el cálculo a cambio: un hombre que no responde también es una respuesta, y no de la clase peligrosa. Siente sus ojos en la espalda hasta que la próxima elevación se lo lleva.

text.en: Answers honestly. No soldiers seen. Watches the hand on the knife-belt relax slightly.
Takes the long way around.
Walks past slowly. Does not give him evidence. Does not correct him.
Maps the location. Continues. This goes in the next report.
Does not slow. Does not look at them directly. Moves with the ease of someone who belongs on this road.
Passes without acknowledging. What they are doing is not her concern. What they will do because of it may be.
Does not stop. Does not show recognition. Files it.
Takes the western branch at the split. Watches them disappear from the eastern treeline.
Stops. Looks at the marked stone. Then looks up at the watcher. Moves the stone to the secondary position. Waits.
Does not approach. Does not startle them. When they look up and see her seeing the marks, she gives them the old sign.
Gives them the acknowledgment sign. Waits.
Tells them what she has seen. Watches them understand what it means.
Asks him what he means by holding. Listens to the answer.
Watches from respectful distance. Does not interrupt. Continues with the information filed.
Meets the look. Moves aside to let him pass.
Does not respond immediately. Then: I know.
Takes the letter. Does not open it while he watches.
Waves back. Continues.
Watches them until they disappear over the hill. Then continues.
Asks which direction they moved. Thanks him. Adjusts the patrol.
Listens to the whole thing. Does not offer hope. Offers: I will remember his name.
Notes the direction. Continues.
Buys the drink. Gets the name.
Continues. Does not stop to watch.
Takes the ford upstream. Adds an hour. They never know he was there.
Identifies where the crossbow must be given the bolt-case position. Plans accordingly.
Notes the duration. Walks past on the far side of the ruin wall. They do not see her.
Counts the men. Notes the captive's condition. Makes a decision.
Reads the tracks. Adjusts the route to keep the ridge on the left.
Does not answer the question. Reads the spacing. Decides which one to move toward.
Hears the difference between kill-on-sight and bring-back. Adjusts accordingly.
Has approximately ten seconds before the captain decides.
Does not change pace. Changes route at the next junction.
Does not look up. Does not slow. Finds cover before the junction.
Has three options. Runs the cost of each. Chooses the one that costs the road least.
Walks the road at the exact pace that makes her uninteresting. Does not look at the hollow.
Lets them decide. Does not volunteer information about the trail.
Reads the timing. Continues on the road knowing what is ahead of them.
Does not go down to the road. Watches until the column passes. Then waits another hour.
Counts them. Identifies the banner. Moves.
Files the banner. Continues. This is not a coincidence.
Does not go down to the road.
Finds the angle. Finds the timing. Decides.
Goes down to the road.
Holds the gaze for the three seconds. Then continues.
Says: I see you. I will remember this road.
Notes what is wrong about the face. Does not indicate it. Continues.
Answers the questions with plausible misdirection. Files the encounter.
Takes the seat across the fire. Speaks first. Watches what the mercenary does with the initiative.
Asks who sends it. The answer is not one she expected.
Stops. Asks on whose authority.
Does not approach the bridge. Looks for the ford.
Answers the first question before it is asked. Watches the captain decide whether the answer fits.
Notes the direction. Continues west.
Uses them correctly.
Does not enter the chamber. Does not reveal presence. Listens.
Asks him where he heard that name. The answer is worse than any she would have constructed herself.
Goes forward. Notes where they would not let them go back.
Has no papers. Has a story instead. Watches to see which one the Man prefers.
Measures the distance to the road's edge. Then measures the distance to the tower he can see behind the patrol. Leaves the road.
Does not run. Running on a snowfield goes badly. Continues at the same pace.
Moves toward the forward exit. Does not run yet.
Sits across the junction. Asks him what he remembers of the forges on the third level.
Listens to what the negotiation is. Does not agree to anything immediately.
Does not step on anything. Does not breathe loudly. Moves around the fire's light.
Answers the question. Tells him the direction. Watches him go.
Thinks about what he can spare. Considers what walking out of the Trollshaws is worth.
Tells him what she is. Asks what he is. He finds this extremely funny.
Does not run. Does not retreat. Stands.
Does not look at the circling one. Keeps eyes on the one that spoke.
Has approximately four options. Three of them are bad.
Looks for what is behind it — what it is guarding. Then looks for the way around.
Produces what papers exist. Watches how he reads them.
Takes the right side. Moves fast.
Acknowledges it. Waits.

label.en: Tell him what became of the tower
label.es: Contarle qué fue de la torre

text.en: A man who asks after his tower deserves the truth about it, told straight, the way he would want it told: rubble, for a hundred and forty years, and the sheep paths run over it now. The warden looks at the ground between them for a long while — long enough for the traveller to understand what it costs to hear a hundred and forty years in one sentence. Then he says, 'I held it until the last stone but one,' and something in the night accepts the truth as payment.
text.es: Un hombre que pregunta por su torre merece la verdad sobre ella, dicha sin rodeos, como a él le gustaría que se la dijeran: escombro, desde hace ciento cuarenta años, y los senderos de las ovejas la pisan ahora. El guardián mira el suelo que hay entre ambos durante un buen rato — lo suficiente para que el viajero entienda lo que cuesta oír ciento cuarenta años en una sola frase. Entonces dice: «La sostuve hasta la penúltima piedra», y algo en la noche acepta la verdad como pago.

label.en: Ask how the tower's last night went
label.es: Preguntar cómo fue la última noche de la torre

text.en: He asks how the tower's last night went — and the dead man tells it the way soldiers tell things: who stood the wall, where the line broke, what the warden said to the men who wanted to run. Not all of it, but enough that the traveller now carries a garrison where an hour ago there was only a shade.
text.es: Pregunta cómo fue la última noche de la torre — y el muerto la cuenta como cuentan los soldados: quién sostuvo la muralla, dónde se rompió la línea, qué les dijo el guardián a los hombres que querían huir. No todo, pero sí lo bastante para que el viajero ahora lleve consigo una guarnición donde hace una hora sólo había una sombra.

label.en: Bow to the dead and leave him his accounting
label.es: Reverencia al muerto y déjalo con sus cuentas

text.en: He bows once — the dead of Arnor are owed that much — and does not answer. Some griefs are not his to settle, and a warden who has kept his post a hundred and forty years will keep it a while longer. The ghost watches him go without anger; perhaps, in the end, not knowing is also a kind of watch.
text.es: Se inclina una vez — a los muertos de Arnor se les debe al menos eso — y no responde. Hay pesares que no le toca saldar, y un guardián que ha mantenido su puesto ciento cuarenta años lo mantendrá un poco más. El fantasma lo mira partir sin enojo; tal vez, al final, no saber también es una forma de guardia.

text.en: Tells her which road leads east. Does not tell her the rest.
Does not engage with the shape. Asks what it actually is.
Asks it what is on this road.
Does not move. Does not flee. Waits for it to speak.
Answers with his name said back at it. Watches whether that matters.
Answers it in the same tongue. Says: so should you.
Does not move toward it. Finds the secondary exit that all Khazad passages have.
Asks what two-footed thing moves at night for three nights in the same area.
Asks which direction it is organized toward.
Asks where the quiet starts.
Tells the raven it is correct. Watches Radagast receive this secondhand.
Tells him what she has felt. Watches him decide what to do with the confirmation.
Accepts the dinner. Does not ask how he knew.
Asks what outside means.
Asks when the questions started.
Continues. Does not look toward the south-east.
Does not look south-east. Does not acknowledge. Continues.
Moves without haste. Does not break branches. Does not take anything.

label.en: Answer the question at its own speed
label.es: Responder la pregunta a su propia velocidad

text.en: The question took the better part of a minute to ask; he gives it the time it deserves to answer — a full minute of standing and thinking, because an Ent can tell an answer from a performance of one. He says he is walking west, that he takes nothing the forest did not offer, and that the road through is old enough to be a custom rather than a trespass. The Ent considers this for a while. Then — with a movement as small as a hill deciding — it lets him pass beneath the branches as something that belongs on the road.
text.es: La pregunta tardó lo suyo en ser formulada; él le dedica el tiempo que merece para responderla — un minuto entero de pie, pensando, porque un Ent sabe distinguir una respuesta de la actuación de una. Dice que camina hacia el oeste, que no toma nada que el bosque no haya ofrecido, y que el camino que la cruza es tan viejo que ya es costumbre y no intrusión. El Ent lo considera un rato. Luego — con un movimiento tan pequeño como una colina decidiendo — lo deja pasar bajo las ramas como algo que pertenece al camino.

label.en: Ask what the forest itself has noticed
label.es: Preguntar qué ha notado el bosque

text.en: He answers, then dares the Ent's own courtesy back at it: and what has the forest noticed? The pause this earns is longer — Entish consideration, not silence. 'Something moves in the deep wood,' it says at last, 'that is not of the forest, and not wholly of the Shadow. The trees do not like its smell.' He files it under the day's real news.
text.es: Responde, y luego se atreve a devolverle al Ent su propia cortesía: ¿y qué ha notado el bosque? La pausa que esto le gana es más larga — consideración entish, no silencio. «Algo se mueve en el bosque profundo», dice por fin, «que no es del bosque, y no enteramente de la Sombra. A los árboles no les gusta su olor». Lo archiva entre las noticias verdaderas del día.

label.en: Bow to the wood and go the long way
label.es: Reverencia al bosque y rodear

text.en: He does not wait out the question. A Dúnadan learns early that some doors are not his to open, and the forest — having watched him choose the long way without complaint — permits the courtesy: the path around is clear, the birdsong continues, and somewhere overhead something that was watching loses interest politely.
text.es: No espera a que la pregunta termine. Un Dúnadan aprende temprano que hay puertas que no le corresponde abrir, y el bosque — tras verlo elegir el camino largo sin queja — le permite la cortesía: el sendero del rodeo está despejado, el canto de los pájaros continúa, y en algún lugar sobre su cabeza algo que lo observaba pierde interés con educación.

text.en: Sits down at its roots. Asks what the forest saw.
Confirms it. Asks what the Ents have seen on the eastern edge recently.
Considers the timeframe. Tells him she was not there at the beginning but knew those who were.
Reads the map. Names what she can. Tells him what the missing landmark was.
Tells them what it is. Watches them decide what to do with that information.
Gives him what food she can spare. Tells him which road is safer.
Does not ask what he found. Walks with him for half a mile. Then lets him go.
Asks whose road this is. Waits to see how he answers.
Answers the first question before he asks it. Watches whether that unsettles him.
Keeps her attention on the Man. Does not look at the orc.
Lets the fear be visible to him. Then walks past.
Tells him the garrison direction. Asks what is on the road behind him.
Asks where the shaft is. Files it.
Notes the direction and the duration. Continues north.
Asks what he knew of that man.
Asks what the old protocols were. Gets an answer he half-remembers.
Does not enter. Listens. Maps the chamber location. Withdraws.
Marks the road on his mental map. Circles wide.
Moves toward the forward exit before they realize he is there.
Thanks them. Notes the mill crossing.
Gives him the honest read of the northern road. Gets his read of the south in return.
Notes what they will not name. Takes it with them.
Trades road conditions. Gets a detailed picture of the next three days.
Listens to the full description. Files the location.
Notes the junction. Notes the direction.
Reads it. Continues.
Tells him what the northern road looked like. Watches him calculate.
Stays still. Does not explain anything until asked.
Tells him the road condition. Does not ask about the letter.
Listens without offering an opinion. That is what is wanted.
Takes the ridge track.
Trades road news. Gets a detailed account of the southern road.
Gives him the northern rumour as he heard it. Gets the southern picture in return.
Notes the direction they came from. Continues north.
Returns the acknowledgment. Continues.
Gives him the western road conditions directly. He nods, thanks them in Rohirric, and rides back.
Asks when the closure will lift. The captain does not know.
Continues without looking up.
Asks what direction the disturbances are coming from.
Asks what they have seen. Gets a partial answer.
Pays the toll. Continues on a better road than most.
Tells him what the southern road looked like at night.

label.en: Trade road-truth for the common-room picture
label.es: Cambiar verdad del camino por el panorama del salón

text.en: He trades what the northern road looked like — honestly, because Bree's exchange rate for truth is the best on this road. In return the full picture arrives: the merchant's story put the orcs two days further east than the track-sign says; the Ranger who left early was heading that way; and the questioner wears a cloak with no maker's mark and asks about travellers by description. Bree currently knows more than it suspects.
text.es: Cambia cómo se veía el camino del norte — con honestidad, porque la tasa de cambio de Bree por la verdad es la mejor de este camino. A cambio llega el panorama completo: el cuento del mercader ponía a los orcos dos días más al este de lo que dice el rastro; el Montaraz que salió temprano iba para ese lado; y el que pregunta usa una capa sin marca de sastre y pregunta por viajeros por descripción. Bree actualmente sabe más de lo que sospecha.

label.en: Ask about the one who asks
label.es: Preguntar por el que pregunta

text.en: He asks about the one asking questions — cloak, voice, who he has spoken to. The Bree woman narrows her eyes, pleased at being asked something worth knowing: 'Asks who came through and what they looked like. Pays in silver. Silver is honest — questions like his usually are not.'
text.es: Pregunta por el que hace preguntas — capa, voz, con quién habló. La mujer de Bree entrecierra los ojos, contenta de que le pregunten algo que vale saber: «Pregunta quién pasó y qué aspecto tenía. Paga en plata. La plata es honesta — las preguntas como las suyas, normalmente no».

label.en: Eat, listen, and add nothing to Bree's account
label.es: Comer, escuchar, y no sumar nada a la cuenta de Bree

text.en: He buys nothing — eats, listens to the room's talk the way a man reads sign, and leaves without adding to Bree's account of him. The woman notes the discretion the way she notes everything, and files him under travellers worth watching for.
text.es: No compra nada — come, escucha la charla del salón como un hombre lee un rastro, y se va sin sumar nada a la cuenta que Bree lleva de él. La mujer anota la discreción como anota todo, y lo archiva bajo viajeros que vale vigilar.

label.en: Ask what kind of questions they asked
label.es: Preguntar qué clase de preguntas hacían

text.en: He asks what kind of questions — the details matter. 'Who came through in the last fortnight. Which way they went. Whether anyone asked after them.' The man says it flat, and flatter still when he adds: 'I told them nothing. But nothing was all I had, and they knew it.' The traveller files the questions under things worth knowing south of Bree.
text.es: Pregunta qué clase de preguntas — los detalles importan. «Quién pasó en la última quincena. Hacia dónde iba. Si alguien preguntaba por él». El hombre lo dice sin inflexión, y más aún cuando agrega: «No les dije nada. Pero nada era todo lo que tenía, y ellos lo sabían». El viajero archiva las preguntas bajo cosas que vale saber al sur de Bree.

label.en: Walk him to the next waymark
label.es: Acompañarlo hasta el próximo hito

text.en: He gives the man what a ranger can give a frightened honest man: 'Walk with me to the next waymark and tell it slower.' The relief that crosses his face is almost embarrassment — Bree pride dies hard, but dying is harder.
text.es: Le da al hombre lo que un montaraz puede darle a un hombre honesto asustado: «Caminá conmigo hasta el próximo hito y contámelo más despacio». El alivio que le cruza la cara es casi vergüenza — el orgullo de Bree muere duro, pero morir es más duro.

label.en: Let him keep his hurry
label.es: Déjalo con su apuro

text.en: He lets the man keep his hurry — a frightened man explains himself best to distance. The nod they exchange carries the whole transaction: nothing asked, nothing owed, good road to him.
text.es: Lo deja con su apuro — un hombre asustado se explica mejor con la distancia. El gesto que cruzan lleva la transacción entera: nada preguntado, nada debido, buen camino.

label.en: Tell them what the east road looked like
label.es: Contarles cómo se veía el camino del este

text.en: He tells them what the eastern road actually looked like — the traffic he saw, where it thinned, the exact stretch that went quiet. They listen the way people listen who have been starved of anything solid, and the oldest nods slowly: 'Three days, and you are the first to come out and say it plain.' Whatever they decide, they decide on his word — and he watches them understand that too.
text.es: Les cuenta cómo se veía realmente el camino del este — el tránsito que vio, dónde raleó, el tramo exacto que quedó en silencio. Escuchan como escucha la gente a la que le han faltado cosas sólidas, y el mayor asiente despacio: «Tres días, y sos el primero que sale y lo dice claro». Decidan lo que decidan, lo decidirán por su palabra — y él los ve entender eso también.

label.en: Sit with them and read the road together
label.es: Sentarse con ellos y leer el camino juntos

text.en: He sits with them a while and reads the road with them — where the wrongness starts, what a watching-man looks for, which hour is worst. When he leaves they are arguing over a turn-back plan like Bree-landers again — which is to say, like people who intend to live.
text.es: Se sienta con ellos un rato y lee el camino junto a ellos — dónde empieza lo que anda mal, qué buscaría un vigía, qué hora es la peor. Cuando se va están discutiendo un plan de regreso como bree-landers otra vez — es decir, como gente que piensa vivir.

label.en: Give the shape of it and keep walking
label.es: Darles el contorno y seguir

text.en: He gives them the road's shape and not an hour of his company — their waiting is theirs to end. As he goes, the argument starts behind him, loud and practical, and it sounds like the first healthy thing on the east road in three days.
text.es: Les da el contorno del camino y no una hora de su compañía — la espera es suya para terminarla. Al irse, la discusión empieza a su espalda, fuerte y práctica, y suena como lo primero sano en el camino del este en tres días.

text.en: Stays at the edge of the firelight. Does not interrupt.
Asks what the something is.
Asks who sent the message. He will not say. Asks what is ahead. He will not say that either.
Takes the offer seriously.
Listens to the description. Carries it.
Accepts the verdict.
Thinks back over the night road. Tells her what was unusual.
Describes the mercenary from the wayhouse two days back. Watches her recognize it.
Continues past. Or stops and asks.
Tells him what was unusual. He listens without interrupting.

label.en: Answer the gate-check and take the warning

text.en: He answers the questions directly and notes the bridge — the western fork is no longer an option he needs to discover. 'Turned out a week back,' the sergeant says, closing the ledger.
